title: Intrinsic (valley) thermal Hall conductivity of phonons in graphene for integer quantum Hall phases
abstract: We calculate the intrinsic contribution to the (valley) thermal Hall conductivity of phonons in (Semenoff-gapped) graphene in the quantum Hall regime where bulk electron thermal transport is suppressed. The (valley) thermal Hall transport of phonons considered here originates from a phonon (valley) Hall viscosity induced by electron (valley) Hall conductivity and viscosity via geometric electron-phonon coupling. The so generated phonon (valley) Hall viscosity is identified with the emergent (valley) Hall viscosity recently introduced in \textit{Phys. Lett. A} \textbf{595}, 132096 (2026). While our calculations refer to graphene, they may very well be generalized to other Dirac materials like group-VI transition metal dichalcogenides. We discuss the prospect of measuring the phonon thermal Hall conductivity in graphene-based heterostructures and estimate the corresponding valley response induced by electrons in the inversion symmetry broken phase.
summary: This theoretical work calculates the intrinsic thermal Hall conductivity of phonons in graphene operating in the quantum Hall regime. It shows that while the direct phonon contribution is small, the valley-specific thermal Hall response mediated by electron-phonon coupling is predicted to be significant. This provides a pathway to experimentally probe valley physics using lattice vibrations in 2D Dirac materials.
main_problem: The paper calculates the intrinsic (valley) thermal Hall conductivity of phonons in graphene when bulk electron thermal transport is suppressed, specifically in the quantum Hall regime.
main_result: While the intrinsic phonon thermal Hall conductivity is predicted to be small, the valley thermal Hall transport induced by electron coupling is predicted to be comparable in size to the charge channel transport, suggesting a measurable valley response.
method: The analysis uses effective field theory and linear response theory, deriving the phonon Hall viscosity by integrating out massive Dirac electrons coupled via geometric electron-phonon coupling.
model_or_system: The system is graphene, modeled using a Dirac fermion formulation for electrons coupled to lattice distortions (phonons). The analysis is performed in the quantum Hall regime, treating the coupling perturbatively.
key_observables: Phonon (valley) thermal Hall conductivity ($\kappa_{ph}^H$, $\kappa_{ph}^{vH}$), Phonon Hall viscosity ($\eta_{	ext{em}}^H$), and the ratio $\kappa_{ph}^H / \kappa_e^H$.
important_parameters: Quantum Hall regime, low temperature ($T 	o 0$), and the magnitude of the electron-phonon coupling ($\partial_{ih}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes graphene can be approximated by its pristine state and relies on low-temperature approximations for the phonon dispersion relation.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the general framework for phonon Hall viscosity induced by electronic Hall effects, deriving the necessary effective actions, and finally calculating the specific intrinsic and valley contributions to the thermal Hall conductivity.
why_interesting: The work connects topological concepts (Hall viscosity, Berry curvature) from electronic transport to lattice dynamics (phonons), providing a theoretical framework for measuring emergent topological responses in condensed matter systems.
